papers.title: Mechanism of GPR84 allosteric modulation at a helix 8-proximate site.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of GPR84 bound to agonist and the positive allosteric modulator PSB-16671 reveal a helix 8-proximate allosteric site. A polar residue network linking orthosteric and allosteric pockets tunes GI-biased signaling, disfavoring beta-arrestin recruitment and sustaining macrophage phagocytosis of cancer cells, suggesting broadly targetable allosteric sites across class A GPCRs.

papers.title: Engineering plant tandem kinase immune receptors expands effector recognition profiles.
papers.summary: The barley and wheat tandem kinase proteins RMO2 and RWT7 recognize different blast fungus effectors via their integrated HMA domains, using distinct protein interfaces with nanomolar affinity. Structure-guided interface substitutions enabled engineering of dual-specificity receptors, establishing integrated HMA domains as programmable modules for designing new disease-resistance specificities in cereal crops.

papers.title: Thalamofrontal synaptic weakening underlies short-term memory deficits from adolescent NMDAR hypofunction.
papers.summary: Repeated adolescent ketamine exposure (NMDAR hypofunction) impaired short-term memory in mice by reducing release probability at mediodorsal thalamus to dorsomedial prefrontal cortex synapses, with diminished direction-selective cortical coding. Chemogenetic strengthening of these projections restored neural selectivity and behavior, identifying a projection-specific presynaptic mechanism behind thalamofrontal dysconnectivity in schizophrenia.

papers.title: Computational design of optimized and preferentially paired human TCR constant regions for improved T cell function.
papers.summary: Using PROSS and FuncLib algorithms, researchers engineered a structurally enhanced TCR (SeT) constant region with improved stability and preferential chain pairing. SeT-expressing T cells showed higher surface expression, functional avidity, cytokine secretion, and cytotoxicity, including in CD4+ T cells, and significantly delayed tumor growth in xenografts across six different TCRs.

papers.title: Transmembrane delivery of antimicrobial peptides by engineered eCIS into macrophages for intracellular mycobacteria elimination.
papers.summary: The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC), an extracellular contractile injection system, was engineered to deliver mycobacteriophage-derived antimicrobial peptides into alveolar macrophages via CD11b targeting. PVC-mediated delivery inhibited intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including an isoniazid-resistant strain, and reduced pulmonary bacterial load more than tenfold in infected mice, alleviating inflammation.

papers.title: Ultrasound-enhanced exosome secretion and antibody-free SERS profiling for Alzheimer's disease via iPSC-derived cortical organoids.
papers.summary: A label-free surface-enhanced Raman scattering platform profiles intact exosomes from iPSC-derived cortical organoids. Optimized ultrasound stimulation increased exosome secretion and upregulated exosome-related genes, enabling discrimination of APOE genotype-specific exosomal fingerprints linked to Alzheimer's pathology, providing a precision-diagnostic framework for neurodegenerative disease without antibody-based markers.

papers.title: Spatial organization of AQP4 water channel expression in the human brain.
papers.summary: Reconstructing whole-brain AQP4 water-channel expression shows a highly organized glymphatic-related topography, peaking in subcortical, ventral, and periventricular territories near CSF reservoirs. AQP4-enriched regions show lower perfusion, colocalize with tau and TDP-43 proteinopathy atrophy patterns, and correspond to glioma hotspots, linking clearance anatomy to neurodegeneration vulnerability.

papers.title: Persistent TOP1 cleavage complexes in drug-tolerant cells drive adaptive resistance to EGFR-targeted therapies in lung cancer.
papers.summary: EGFR inhibition in EGFR-mutated lung cancer downregulates TDP1, impairing repair of topoisomerase I cleavage complexes (TOP1ccs). In drug-tolerant cells, elevated ROS drives TOP1cc accumulation, mutation acquisition, and reproliferation. TDP1 is absent in roughly 25% of EGFR-mutant lung cancers, and combining EGFR inhibitors with sublethal topotecan abolished reproliferation in TDP1-deficient cells.

papers.title: The effect of microgravity and flows on the organization and dynamics of the human genome.
papers.summary: Simulated microgravity altered nuclear shape and size and visibly affected nucleolar liquid phases, but genome organization and dynamics remained largely preserved, and microgravity—unlike flows—caused no DNA damage. The findings demonstrate robustness of genome architecture against mechanical stress and clarify gravity's role in nuclear function relevant to spaceflight biology.

papers.title: An ASXL3-thyroid hormone axis in parvalbumin interneurons controls autism-like behaviors.
papers.summary: ASXL3 haploinsufficiency in mice derepresses the thyroid hormone-inactivating enzyme DIO3 via altered H2A monoubiquitination, depleting brain thyroid hormone and expanding parvalbumin interneurons, producing autism-like behaviors. Neonatal, but not adolescent, thyroid hormone supplementation rescued interneuron numbers and behavior, and an intein-based AAV system restoring full-length ASXL3 normalized cortical architecture and behavior.

papers.title: High-fidelity genotyping and therapeutic oligonucleotides analysis by liquid-phase ion trap coupled with mass spectrometry.
papers.summary: A liquid-phase ion trap (LPIT) system uses strong electric fields to dissociate metal contaminants and enrich nucleic acid ions directly in solution, improving mass accuracy up to 48-fold and signal intensity 100-fold for intact DNA. Applications include high-resolution genotyping, rapid influenza subtyping from raw PCR products, and impurity detection in therapeutic oligonucleotides.

papers.title: Dietary α-ketoglutarate modulates lung adenocarcinoma growth and epigenetic remodeling in a sex-dependent fashion.
papers.summary: Dietary calcium alpha-ketoglutarate remodeled lung adenocarcinoma in mice in a sex-dependent manner: female mice showed reduced tumor area with decreased repressive histone marks and upregulated TBX5, whereas male mice showed increased tumor area and elevated H3K27me3. In human lung adenocarcinoma, TBX5 enrichment in female tumors associated with improved survival.

papers.title: Alternate day fasting attenuates metabolic dysfunction-associated arterial thrombotic risk via increasing indole-3-propionic acid.
papers.summary: Alternate day fasting attenuated platelet hyperreactivity and thrombotic tendency in obese mice by reshaping gut microbiota. The microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid preserved intraplatelet Rho GTPase cycle homeostasis, suppressing platelet activation without affecting hemostasis. Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated arterial thrombosis showed lower plasma IPA levels, predicting thrombotic risk inversely correlated with platelet reactivity.

papers.title: piRNA-mediated silencing of exogenous retrovirus in mouse spermatogonial stem cells.
papers.summary: In mouse spermatogonial stem cells, transient viral infection induces piRNAs that silence exogenous retrovirus; this defense is perturbed in TRP53- or PIWIL2-deficient cells, reducing H3K9me3 and DNA methylation at long terminal repeats. The study defines a piRNA-MAGEA5-TRP53 axis that restricts viral invasion and preserves germline genome integrity.

papers.title: Mitotic assembly of respiratory supercomplexes ensures accurate cell division and fuels tumor growth.
papers.summary: Assembly of mitochondrial respiratory supercomplexes (complexes I, III, IV) is markedly enhanced during mitosis in cancer cells, driven by CDK1-promoted translation of NDUFA3. Disrupting supercomplex assembly caused ROS accumulation, mitotic cell death, and chromosome segregation defects, and inhibiting the process suppressed tumor growth in vivo.

papers.title: SUCLG2 contributes to platinum resistance in lung adenocarcinoma through enhancing succinylation of GAC and glutamine metabolism.
papers.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
papers.summary: SUCLG2, the beta subunit of succinyl-CoA synthetase, contributes to platinum resistance in lung adenocarcinoma by promoting glutamine metabolism and succinylating glutaminase (GAC), enhancing its activity, reducing ROS, and suppressing apoptosis. SUCLG2 knockout sensitized cells to platinum drugs, and knockout enhanced sensitivity in animal models, marking SUCLG2 as a resistance driver and target.

papers.title: GLG1 in cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes bladder cancer growth while limiting tumor apoptosis.
papers.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
papers.summary: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing of bladder cancer with Mendelian randomization and colocalization, the study prioritizes GLG1, a fibroblast-enriched gene. GLG1 was higher in tumor tissues, associated with invasiveness, and upregulated in fibroblasts via tumor-derived TGF-beta/SMAD2/3 signaling. Caf-conditioned medium effects and xenograft modeling support GLG1-mediated tumor-stromal crosstalk promoting bladder cancer growth.

papers.title: Targeting LAMP2 synergizes with gemcitabine to inhibit bladder cancer progression via modulating STING degradation and regulating macrophage phenotypes.
papers.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
papers.summary: LAMP2 drives STING ubiquitination and lysosomal degradation in bladder cancer via p62-mediated macroautophagy and HSC70-dependent chaperone-mediated autophagy. The LAMP2-binding small molecule MM-2, discovered by virtual screening, combined with gemcitabine blocked autophagic flux, activated STING signaling, and shifted tumor-associated macrophage phenotypes, implicating the LAMP2-STING-TAM axis as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: A guide to transcriptional cyclin-dependent kinases in cancer.
papers.summary: This review summarizes how transcriptional cyclin-dependent kinases (tCDKs) control RNA polymerase II activity across the transcription cycle, how their dysregulation drives oncogenic phenotypes, and recent development of tCDK inhibitors and degraders in preclinical models and clinical trials, where notable successes have recently been reported across a spectrum of human cancers.

papers.title: Univariate-guided sparse regression for Biobank-scale high-dimensional omics data.
papers.summary: UniLasso is a two-stage penalized regression for polygenic risk scores adapted to UK Biobank scale, extended as UniLasso-ES to incorporate external summary statistics guiding penalty weights and sign constraints. It matches standard lasso predictive performance while selecting substantially fewer variants, remaining competitive with PRS-CS and lassosum2.

papers.title: Drosophila heat shock factor (HSF) regulates developmental growth by maintaining the basal expression of HSP83/HSP90.
papers.summary: Drosophila heat shock factor null larvae arrest at early second instar with reduced basal HSP83/HSP90. Tissue-specific knockdown revealed organ-specific developmental requirements—endoreplication and growth defects, wing abnormalities, follicle degeneration, melanotic tumors—and restoring HSP83 expression partially or fully rescued these defects, establishing basal chaperone expression as HSF's key developmental effector.

papers.title: Toll-like Receptor 2 Recognition of Microbiota Lipoproteins and Lipids in Immunity and Therapy.
papers.summary: This review covers Toll-like receptor 2 recognition of microbiota-derived ligands beyond canonical bacterial lipoproteins, including lipids, proteins, and polysaccharides. Chemical biology and structural studies show how subtle ligand architecture variations influence TLR2 heterodimer usage, downstream signaling, and context-dependent immune outcomes, informing development of synthetic TLR2 agonists for immunity and therapy.

papers.title: METTL3‑mediated OTUB1 sustains PD‑L1 protein stability via deubiquitination and promotes immune evasion in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.summary: In oral squamous cell carcinoma, METTL3-mediated m6A modification stabilizes OTUB1 mRNA via the reader YTHDF1. OTUB1 deubiquitinates PD-L1, sustaining its protein stability and PD-1 binding. OTUB1 knockdown enhanced T cell infiltration and tumor cell apoptosis in co-culture and mouse models, identifying a METTL3-OTUB1-PD-L1 axis promoting immune evasion.

papers.title: Mitotically driven cytoskeletal reorganization governs zebrafish left-right organizer detachment from EVL and lumen morphogenesis.
papers.summary: In zebrafish Kupffer's vesicle formation, dorsal forerunner cells attach to the enveloping layer independently of mitosis, but cytokinetic bridges and associated microtubule bundles recruit actin, seed rosette centers, and drive detachment and lumen formation. Disrupting early, not later, divisions impaired these events, revealing how division history directs epithelial assembly.

papers.title: Distinct mechanism of syntaxin3-dependent tight junction assembly in keratinocyte model cells.
papers.summary: In differentiated HaCaT keratinocytes, syntaxin3 lacking the apical targeting signal still induces tight junction assembly, unlike in simple epithelia. A differentiation-induced extracellularly exposed subpopulation of syntaxin3 appears crucial, with a six-amino-acid motif in helix B essential, revealing a distinct SNARE-dependent mechanism of tight junction assembly in epidermal barrier formation.

papers.title: Use of faricimab for refractory diabetic macular edema in real-world clinical practice: When anatomical success meets functional limits.
papers.summary: In this retrospective real-world study of 110 eyes, faricimab significantly reduced central macular thickness in both treatment-naive and refractory diabetic macular edema over 12 months. Visual acuity improved significantly in naive eyes but only marginally in refractory eyes, which had higher baseline DRIL and ELM/ellipsoid zone disruption, limiting functional gains despite anatomical success.

papers.title: Phase response curve and RNA-sequencing demonstrate spiders' sensitivity to light and pinpoint candidate light-responsive genes.
papers.summary: A type 0 phase response curve for the orb-weaver spider Metazygia wittfeldae shows high-amplitude phase shifts to one-hour light pulses, with a break point around circadian time 16-18. RNA-seq identified light-pulse-responsive genes, many downregulated one hour after the pulse with flipped expression nine hours later, plus clock gene homologs with atypical arthropod patterns.

papers.title: The limited role of RGS10 on NFκB and cytokine transcript levels in peritoneal macrophages under the influence of opioid analgesics.
papers.summary: In peritoneal macrophages from RGS10 knockout mice studied in the presence of opioid analgesics, RGS10 showed limited, transient influence on NFkappaB subunit and cytokine transcript levels but more robust negative regulation of secreted pro-inflammatory cytokine proteins, indicating its regulatory role manifests predominantly at the protein rather than transcript level.

papers.title: Design of a high-affinity IL-21 decoy receptor as a novel therapeutic strategy for autoimmune disorders.
papers.summary: Using the extracellular domain of the IL-21 receptor as a scaffold, five binding-site residues were computationally mutated to create a decoy receptor. The Q33S/E38D/M70T/L94N/M130S mutant retained structure, was expressed in E. coli, and showed 1.4-fold higher IL-21 binding affinity than wild type by SPR (KD 50 pM), supporting autoimmune therapy potential.

papers.title: Emerging roles of SLC6A14 in digestive system diseases: from amino acid transport to therapeutic targeting.
papers.summary: This review summarizes SLC6A14, a Na+/Cl--dependent amino acid transporter with broad substrate specificity, and its context-dependent roles in inflammatory bowel disease, cystic fibrosis-associated gastrointestinal phenotypes, and digestive cancers including gastric, colorectal, and pancreatic cancers, affecting epithelial injury, fluid secretion, and tumor proliferation, with potential as biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Targeting the METTL5-MGST1 axis for cancer therapy: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.summary: This review examines the METTL5-MGST1 axis: METTL5, an 18S rRNA m6A methyltransferase stabilized by TRMT112, methylates the decoding-center adenosine 1832 to orchestrate oncogenic mRNA translation, while MGST1 mediates ferroptosis suppression and redox homeostasis. The axis is implicated in tumor progression, ferroptosis resistance, immune evasion, and treatment-refractory behavior, most established in hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.title: CBX3 aggravates nucleus pulposus cell apoptosis and extracellular matrix degradation in vitro via repressing SESN2-mediated mitophagy in an H3K9me3-dependent manner.
papers.summary: In an IL-1beta-induced intervertebral disc degeneration model, CBX3 was upregulated in nucleus pulposus cells; its knockdown reduced apoptosis and extracellular matrix degradation and restored PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy. Mechanistically, CBX3 transcriptionally repressed SESN2 in an H3K9me3-dependent manner, and the mitophagy inhibitor MDivi-1 reversed the protective effects of CBX3 knockdown.

papers.title: Overcoming ABT-737 resistance in triple-negative breast cancer: C-phycocyanin-mediated myeloid cell leukemia-1 downregulation enhances apoptotic sensitivity.
papers.summary: In MDA-MB-468 triple-negative breast cancer cells, the BH3-mimetic ABT-737 alone increased MCL-1 by roughly 40%, driving resistance. C-phycocyanin downregulated MCL-1 and BCL-2, upregulated BAK and P53, and synergized with ABT-737 (combination index below 1), lowering IC50 values, inhibiting migration and colony formation, and enhancing caspase-3 activation.

papers.title: Targeting snake venom metalloproteinases: structural diversity, molecular pathogenesis and therapeutic interventions.
papers.summary: This review covers snake venom metalloproteinases (SVMPs), Zn2+-dependent metzincins driving hemorrhage and edema, classified P-I to P-III by domain architecture. With antivenom limitations, targeted neutralization strategies include phytocompounds, small-molecule inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, and nanobodies, while CRISPR-engineered venom gland organoids and AI-assisted screening enable rational therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Unravelling the expression patterns of the CCO gene family in Barley (Hordeum vulgare) under various stress conditions.
papers.summary: A genome-wide analysis identified 11 HvCCO genes in barley, classified into CCD, CCDL, and NCED subfamilies, with conserved structures and motifs. Promoter analysis found 190 cis-regulatory elements; segmental duplication drove family expansion under purifying selection. Twelve miRNAs may regulate HvCCO genes, with tissue-specific and stress-responsive expression patterns from RNA-seq datasets.

papers.title: In vitro evaluation of the Anticarcinogenic effects of zerumbone in the SK-UT-1 human uterine Leiomyosarcoma cell line.
papers.summary: Zerumbone reduced viability of SK-UT-1 human uterine leiomyosarcoma cells in dose- and time-dependent manners, induced G0/G1-phase arrest, and triggered apoptosis while suppressing proliferation. As the first antiproliferative evaluation in this cell line, the data support zerumbone as a candidate therapeutic agent warranting further investigation for uterine leiomyosarcoma.

papers.title: Temporal miRNA remodeling defines a 24-hour regulatory threshold for immune-inflammatory activation in intermittent hypoxia-induced cardiomyocyte injury.
papers.summary: In H9c2 cardiomyocytes exposed to intermittent hypoxia, a hallmark of obstructive sleep apnea, injury severity increased with mitochondrial depolarization, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and caspase-3 apoptosis. No differentially expressed miRNAs appeared at 8 hours, whereas 18 emerged at 24 hours, defining a 24-hour threshold for miRNA-mediated immune-inflammatory remodeling, with miR-146b-5p functionally validated.

papers.title: Selection for Folding Stability Predicts Observed Covariation Between Protein Positions in the PDB.
papers.summary: Using a stability-constrained model of protein evolution, the authors predict statistical couplings between protein positions from selection for folding stability against unfolding and misfolding. Predicted couplings relate explicitly to contact energies, sequence separation, and buriedness, and match observed covariation in PDB structures, supporting folding stability as the selective force generating coevolutionary signals.

papers.title: Mitogenomic Insights into the Tinfoil Barb Barbonymus schwanefeldii from Sumatra, Indonesia: Structural Features, Selective Pressure, Genetic Diversity, and Phylogenetic Placement.
papers.summary: The first mitogenome characterization of the tinfoil barb (Barbonymus schwanefeldii) from Sumatra reveals a 16,578 bp genome with 37 genes, 57.03% AT bias, and strong purifying selection across all 13 protein-coding genes, with positive selection confined to few sites. Most tRNAs retain canonical cloverleaf structures, aiding conservation and phylogenetic placement.

papers.title: NRB-FusePS: A Protein Language Model-Based Multimodal Framework for Predicting Ligand-Binding Residues in Nuclear Receptors.
papers.summary: NRB-FusePS is a protein language model-based multimodal framework predicting ligand-binding residues in nuclear receptors, integrating sequence statistics, structural descriptors, and ESM2 embeddings with protein-level probability smoothing. On an independent protein-level test set it achieved AUC 0.814 and MCC 0.406, with SHAP analysis identifying ESM2 as the main information source.

papers.title: Itaconation and Succination as Metabolite-Derived Cysteine Modifications in Inflammatory Signalling: Biochemical Mechanisms, Chemoproteomic Mapping, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.summary: This review distinguishes itaconation, driven by ACOD1-dependent itaconate, from succination, driven by fumarate accumulation, as metabolite-derived cysteine modifications in inflammatory signaling, covering their differing chemical stability, sources, and functional outcomes including KEAP1-NRF2 signaling, inflammasome regulation, and pyroptosis, and emphasizes distinguishing endogenous metabolites from electrophilic derivatives in pharmacological interpretation.

papers.title: Computational Design Of A Peptide Candidate Targeting NOTCH1 And PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathways In Cancer: A Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics Simulation Study.
papers.summary: Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics and docking, researchers fused a five-amino-acid anticancer motif from dermaseptin-B2 with a ten-amino-acid membrane-active fragment of magainin-2, then introduced three substitutions to generate the lead peptide MD3. Docking showed favorable binding of MD3 to proteins in the PI3K/AKT and NOTCH1 signaling pathways, supporting its anticancer candidacy.

papers.title: Impact of Tramadol Administration on Stomach and Duodenum of Male Rats: Histological Examinations, DNA and Biochemical Analyses.
papers.summary: In male rats, prolonged tramadol administration over weeks induced gastric dysfunction and duodenal injury, disturbed enzymes and hormones including trypsin, pepsin, testosterone, and TNF-alpha, caused detectable DNA damage by comet assay, and generated degeneration in endogenous antioxidant defense mechanisms, demonstrating gastrointestinal and genotoxic consequences of chronic tramadol exposure.
